research_page.title: Donanemab in early Alzheimer's disease (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2)
research_page.description: Phase 3 trial showing donanemab slows clinical decline and clears amyloid plaques in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, alongside high rates of ARIA.
research_page.takeaway_md: In a pivotal Phase 3 trial, donanemab significantly slowed clinical decline and robustly cleared brain amyloid plaques over 76 weeks in patients with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease. This biomarker and clinical efficacy supported its 2024 FDA approval, though the drug is accompanied by a substantial risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).
key_findings_md: Donanemab slowed clinical decline compared to placebo on the iADRS score (difference of +2.92 points, p<0.001) in the overall population (ClinicalTrials.gov).
Treatment profoundly reduced brain amyloid plaque burden by an average of 86.37 Centiloids compared to placebo (ClinicalTrials.gov).
ARIA-E (edema) occurred in 23.4% (200/853) of donanemab participants versus 1.9% (17/874) on placebo, and ARIA-H (microhemorrhages) occurred in 19.5% vs. 7.4% (ClinicalTrials.gov).
Infusion-related reactions were noticeably higher in the donanemab arm at 8.6% (73/853) compared to 0.5% (4/874) for placebo (ClinicalTrials.gov).
research_page.methods_md: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 was a Phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial enrolling 1,736 participants aged 60 to 85. Eligible patients had early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease (prodromal to mild dementia) with positive amyloid and tau PET scans. Participants received intravenous donanemab or placebo every four weeks for up to 76 weeks.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: This study provides the pivotal evidence for donanemab, corroborating earlier Phase 2 findings and establishing robust proof of clinical and biomarker efficacy. The statistically significant slowing of decline directly led to the FDA approval of Kisunla (donanemab-azbt) in July 2024. The safety profile is consistent with the established class-effect risks of anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception of donanemab is heavily polarized. Retail investors and mainstream headlines often frame the drug enthusiastically as a major therapeutic breakthrough, while patients and caregivers balance a desperate hope for delayed disease progression against significant anxiety regarding ARIA and logistical burdens (like MRI monitoring). Scientists and medical professionals maintain a more measured stance, weighing the impressive plaque clearance against the modest clinical benefit and serious safety risks.
caveats_md: The clinical meaningfulness of a 2.92-point change on the 144-point iADRS scale over 18 months remains heavily debated among clinicians.
The registry extract lacks demographic data, making it difficult to assess how well the findings generalize across diverse populations.

While deaths directly attributed to the drug are not fully detailed in the registry top-line, the higher overall rate of ARIA practically necessitates strict, burdensome monitoring protocols in real-world clinical use.

trial_pages.title: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
trial_pages.description: Pivotal Phase 3 trial evaluating donanemab in patients with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.population: 1,736 participants 60 to 85 years old with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease and positive amyloid and tau PET scans.
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS)
trial_pages.why_md: This pivotal trial was designed to confirm whether donanemab could successfully clear amyloid plaques and significantly slow clinical decline in patients with early-stage Alzheimer's. Its results formed the basis for the 2024 FDA approval of Kisunla.
trial_pages.results_md: Donanemab successfully met its primary endpoint, slowing clinical decline on the iADRS by 2.92 points compared to placebo at week 76. It also resulted in profound brain amyloid clearance (-86.37 Centiloids). However, ARIA-E occurred in 23.4% of patients receiving the drug, compared to 1.9% on placebo.

trial_pages.title: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ
trial_pages.description: Phase 2 proof-of-concept trial evaluating donanemab in early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.population: 272 participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) Score
trial_pages.why_md: This Phase 2 trial tested whether donanemab could effectively clear amyloid plaques and alter clinical disease trajectory, establishing proof-of-concept and laying the groundwork for the pivotal TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 study.
trial_pages.results_md: Donanemab slowed cognitive and functional decline on the iADRS score and demonstrated rapid amyloid plaque clearance compared to placebo, establishing robust clinical proof-of-concept for the drug.

timeline_entries.title: 2021-03 — Donanemab Phase 2 results published
timeline_entries.body_md: The [TRAILBLAZER-ALZ](/trials/trailblazer-alz-nct03367403) trial establishes clinical proof-of-concept for donanemab's ability to clear amyloid and modestly slow cognitive decline.

timeline_entries.body_md: Full results from the pivotal [TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2](/research/papers/donanemab-trailblazer-alz-2) trial demonstrate donanemab slows clinical decline while robustly clearing amyloid plaques.
